PROFESSIONAL PORTRAITS · 9 MIN

Professional Headshot Prompts That Preserve Identity.

How to improve wardrobe, background and light without producing a different person.

Published September 3, 2026Editorial team · PromptStudio AI

A successful AI headshot should look like the same person on a very good professional day—not a polished stranger. Identity protection is therefore the first instruction, not an afterthought.

IN THIS GUIDE1. Start with a suitable reference2. Separate identity from presentation3. Match the profession and context4. Perform an identity audit

Start with a suitable reference

Use a sharp photograph with the entire face visible, neutral light and no strong beauty filter. Avoid sunglasses, extreme wide-angle selfies and hair covering important facial landmarks. A model cannot preserve information that the source does not clearly provide.

The reference does not need a studio background. A simple phone photograph can work when eyes, jawline, hairline and skin tone are visible. Use the highest-resolution original rather than a screenshot downloaded from social media.

Separate identity from presentation

List what must remain unchanged: facial structure, eye shape, nose, smile, age, skin tone, hairline and any distinctive features. Then describe what may change: wardrobe, background, lighting, crop and posture.

Avoid instructions such as “make me more attractive” or “perfect the face.” They invite structural changes. Ask instead for even lighting, natural skin texture, temporary blemish reduction and a confident but authentic expression.

Match the profession and context

A technology founder may suit a smart-casual portrait with a contemporary workspace. A financial adviser may need restrained tailoring and a neutral studio. A therapist may benefit from warm window light and a calm environment. The goal is not to stereotype a profession but to align visual signals with audience expectations.

Create a vertical master with room around the shoulders, then crop versions for LinkedIn, speaker pages and company directories. Keep the face large enough to remain recognizable in a small circular avatar.

Perform an identity audit

Compare the result with the source side by side. Check eye spacing, eyelids, smile shape, teeth, ears, hairline, skin tone and apparent age. Reject outputs that look more glamorous but less accurate.

Disclose synthetic or heavily edited portraits when context requires it. Never create professional images of another real person without permission.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
  • Use a clear unfiltered source.
  • Protect identity before changing style.
  • Choose industry-appropriate presentation.
  • Generate for multiple crops.
  • Reject flattering but inaccurate results.
